This pane shows a mesh shader's DXIL, not reflection output. Compiler Explorer
runs dxc.exe, which never calls ID3D12ShaderReflection, so no pane can answer
the question this issue actually asks. What the pane can show is that both
facts the reporter wanted are present in the compiled container.

Scroll to the metadata at the bottom, to the named list of entry points. The
last operand of the entry point is a tag list; the entry with tag number 9
holds the mesh-shader state, and its operand tuple has five fields in this
order: thread group size, max vertex count, max primitive count, output
topology, payload size. Read that tuple against the two attributes at the top
of the shader and every field lines up.

The declared thread group size appears as a nested three-element tuple, and
the fourth field of the mesh state carries the output topology as an integer
enum value, where 1 is line and 2 is triangle.
